decisions.quote: In addition, Ruiz et al. [ 15 ] also detected that rs190982 could decrease the risk of AD through multiple test in a large Spanish sample (OR = 0.885, 95%CI = 0.81 1-0.966). Several factors may be responsible for these discrepancies in these researches.
decisions.reason: Primary Discussion specifically contrasts the current Chinese association results with Ruiz2014Spanishprotective-association result and discusses discrepancies; it is stronger than background-only citation or meta-analysis membership. However, Ruiz and shippedLambert2013report the same rs190982protective finding in a follow-up chain, and current study selects LambertGWASas discovery target. The closest-actual-finding rule versus separate independent follow-up paper cannot be settled by different authors/DOI or pooled meta-analysis alone. Initial categorical exclusion omits contrary own-result comparison; no third unchanged model attempt. Preserve an actual additional-target/chain ambiguity and do not falsely certify a genuinely absent pair or background exclusion.

expert_decision_not_adopted.quote: Recently, a large meta-analysis has confirmed that the SNP rs190982 polymorphism within MEF2C on chromosome 5 acted as a protective factor for AD dementia (OR = 0.93, 95%CI = 0.90-0.95, P = 3.2×10 −8 ) in the Caucasian population [ 14 ]. Similarly, the association between the MEF2C gene rs190982 polymorphism and AD was also confirmed in a large Spanish sample (OR = 0.885, 95%CI = 0.811-0.966) [ 15 ]. Furthermore, another two studies replicated the association in China Han. Regretfully, they failed to reveal any association of rs190982 polymorphism in MEF2C gene with AD susceptibility in our Han Chinese cohort [ 16 , 17 ]. Here, we conducted a case-control study containing 2332 individuals to clarify whether the selected SNP on MEF2C gene has an association with LOAD in Northern Han Chinese population.
expert_decision_not_adopted.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent. The primary replication target of Tang et al. (2016) is the IGAP GWAS discovery of the protective MEF2C rs190982 association with late-onset Alzheimer's disease in 74,046 Caucasians reported by Lambert et al. (2013) [14], which is already represented by shipped row 1136 (10.1038/ng.2802) and singled out in both the Abstract ('identified to be related to late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD) in Caucasians in a large meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies (GWAS)') and the Discussion sample-size comparison ('Caucasian 74 046 vs. Chinese 4089'). Ruiz et al. (2014) [15] ('Follow-up of loci from the International Genomics of Alzheimer's Disease Project identifies TRIP4 as a novel susceptibility gene', 10.1038/tp.2014.2) is an earlier follow-up/replication of the IGAP loci in a Spanish sample, grouped in the Introduction with two prior Chinese replication studies [16, 17] ('Furthermore, another two studies replicated the association in China Han') and in Methods as one of the 'other reports on the associations between MEF2C (rs190982) and LOAD [ 15 – 17 ]' pooled with [14] in the secondary meta-analysis.
